regional.syndrome: Fever, headache, backache, rash and occasional mild meningism; self-limiting.
regional.headline: Highly prevalent African orthobunyavirus causing undifferentiated fever; seroprevalence exceeds 50% in parts of East Africa.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Fever with rash; isolated reports of meningoencephalitis and haemorrhagic manifestations.
regional.headline: Bunyamwera-serogroup virus isolated from African febrile patients, with rare reports of haemorrhagic and neurological presentations.
regional.geography: West, Central and East Africa, Madagascar.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Biphasic: an initial fever with headache and myalgia, brief remission, then in ~15% a toxic phase with jaundice, haemorrhage, renal failure and shock; case fatality in the toxic phase is 30–60%.
regional.headline: The prototype flavivirus and the reason the genus is named 'flavi' — a vaccine-preventable viral haemorrhagic fever.
regional.prevention: A single dose of the 17D live-attenuated vaccine gives lifelong protection — one of the most effective vaccines ever made; mandated under International Health Regulations for travel to endemic areas.
regional.geography: Tropical South America and sub-Saharan Africa.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Fever, lymphadenopathy (a feature distinguishing it from smallpox-like illness without nodes) and a deep-seated vesiculopustular rash, often anogenital and oropharyngeal in sexually transmitted clade IIb infection. Proctitis, severe pain and bacterial superinfection are common; severe disease occurs in advanced HIV.
regional.headline: Orthopoxvirus causing mpox; clade I is more virulent, clade II drove the 2022 global outbreak through sexual networks.
regional.prevention: MVA-BN (JYNNEOS/Imvanex) vaccination pre- and post-exposure; isolation of lesions.
regional.geography: Endemic in Central and West Africa; global clade IIb outbreak since 2022 and clade Ib expansion from eastern DRC since 2023.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Abrupt fever, profound weakness, myalgia, then vomiting and high-volume diarrhoea with electrolyte derangement, shock and sometimes haemorrhage. Survivors experience uveitis, arthralgia and neurological sequelae; virus persists in semen, aqueous humour and CSF, enabling late sexual transmission and relapse.
regional.headline: Filovirus causing Ebola disease, with case fatality historically 25–90%; now treatable with monoclonal antibodies and preventable by vaccination.
regional.prevention: The rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine (Ervebo) used in ring vaccination, plus the Ad26/MVA regimen; safe burial practices and infection prevention and control.
regional.geography: Central and West Africa — the 2013–2016 West African epidemic caused over 28,000 cases.
regional.evidence_note: Virus, viral RNA or specific antibody found in the reservoir host or in livestock, with no human case reported. The virus is present in the country; whether it has ever infected a person there is unknown.

regional.headline: Zoonotic phlebovirus causing devastating ruminant abortion storms and human haemorrhagic fever; a WHO priority pathogen.
